Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

For the first desktop voice-input slice, I would keep the UI small and make the STT backend pluggable from day one instead of hard-wiring browser/OS dictation.

A practical MVP shape:

- push-to-talk button records audio in the desktop app
- audio is sent to an app-side transcription provider, not directly from the renderer to a third-party URL
- transcript is inserted into the prompt box for review/edit by default, instead of auto-sending
- provider config supports a local OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint plus optional model/language fields
- OS dictation/Web Speech can stay as a fallback, but should be visibly distinct from a configured local/private STT provider

That provider boundary would let users run Whisper-compatible services, FunASR/SenseVoice, or other local ASR engines without OpenCode needing to embed each model runtime. It also matters for CJK/local/offline workflows where browser dictation is usually the wrong default.

Tests I would want around the first pass:

- provider API keys/base URLs are not exposed to the renderer when an app-side bridge is used
- failed transcription keeps the recorded audio or draft state intact
- language/model options are forwarded
- transcript insertion is reviewable before send
- local provider and cloud provider paths share the same UI contract

## Proposed readiness semantics

The supervisor should expose a **drain wait** for plugin activation. When Session execution waits, the supervisor must finish the current generation and also apply any plugin/config registrations requested while that generation was activating. It returns only when `requested === applied` at the completion boundary. A registration after that boundary belongs to the next synchronization.

```text
requested = 1
start generation 1
plugin B registers -> requested = 2
finish generation 1
activate generation 2
finish generation 2
requested === applied === 2 -> return
```

This is not a promise that the whole process is globally quiet. Readiness means:

- every included plugin module was imported
- every included plugin's top-level setup returned
- awaited agent, model, command, skill, tool, and hook contributions were registered
- the activation batch committed its state projections
- final config projection plugins ran
- no tracked plugin reload was pending when the wait completed

Readiness does **not** mean:

- arbitrary background fibers completed
- MCP servers connected
- ongoing listeners terminated
- future plugin registrations cannot occur
- network refreshes forked by plugins completed

This implies a plugin contract: **top-level setup must await every initial contribution required for correct Session execution. It may fork only ongoing listeners and later refresh work.** For example, an initial provider refresh needed to construct the catalog must be awaited; the listener for future credential changes should be forked.

Session execution should call this wait before resolving its agent, model, instructions, or tools. After the wait, an explicitly selected missing agent fails with a typed `AgentNotFoundError`; it never proceeds with `permissions: undefined` or falls back to another agent.

Location acquisition and TUI bootstrap remain progressive. They do not wait. This keeps first paint fast while giving model execution the stronger consistency contract it requires.

Considered and deferred: a type-level fix that makes the divergent shape unrepresentable.

A schema combinator can make `workspaceID` a required key whose value may be undefined (optional on the wire, required in the Type):

```ts
const requiredUndefinedOr = <S extends Schema.Top>(schema: S) =>
  Schema.optionalKey(schema).pipe(
    Schema.decodeTo(Schema.UndefinedOr(Schema.toType(schema)), {
      decode: SchemaGetter.withDefault<S["Type"] | undefined>(Effect.succeed(undefined)),
      encode: SchemaGetter.transformOptional(Option.filter((value) => value !== undefined)),
    }),
  )
```

Verified against the repo's effect version: `Ref.make({ directory })` becomes a compile error, decoded payloads always carry the key (so they compare Equal to `requestRef` output), and encoding strips undefined so the wire format is unchanged. About 47 call sites (mostly tests) would need `workspaceID: undefined` added, all surfaced by the compiler.

Deferred because `Equal.equals` and hash-keyed collections appear nowhere else in V2 src, so the `LocationServiceMap` LayerMap is the only Equal-keyed consumer of `Location.Ref`, and #35757 canonicalizes that boundary at runtime, including structural supersets (extra own keys) that the type system cannot rule out. If a second Equal-keyed use of `Location.Ref` appears (for example when workspace placement becomes real), revisit this combinator then. The runtime backstop in #35757 should stay either way.

Notes for whoever picks it up: the canonical key-absent direction is not enforceable without `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, which the repo does not enable, and `Schema.Class`/`Data.Class` do not help since their Equal compares own key sets. `RcMap`/`LayerMap` accept no custom key equivalence.

我查阅日志后定位到两个任务中断的根源问题：
初始请求超时问题：通过新增配置 provider:{"options":{"timeout":6000,"headerTimeout":false,"chunkTimeout":60000}} 调整超时参数，解决了链路超时报错；
Git 版本兼容问题：旧版 Git 不支持--sparse稀疏克隆参数，执行拉取流程时直接中断，升级 Git 版本后兼容该参数。
目前已完成超时参数配置调整与 Git 版本升级，两处问题均修复，流程运行正常。

After checking the logs, I found two root causes leading to task interruption:
Initial request timeout issue: I added the config provider:{"options":{"timeout":6000,"headerTimeout":false,"chunkTimeout":60000}} to adjust timeout parameters, which fixed the link timeout errors.
Git compatibility issue: The old Git version did not support the --sparse flag and broke the clone process. I upgraded Git to a newer compatible version.
Both issues have been resolved by configuring the timeout options and updating Git, and the workflow runs smoothly now.

I can reproduce a server-side memory growth case with the current CLI on Linux. This is not exactly the Windows `CLOSE_WAIT` shape from #22198, but it points at the same event/SSE area and produced an EventTarget listener leak warning.

Environment:

```text
opencode version: 1.17.13
os: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic x64
distro: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
terminal: xterm-256color
plugins: none
mode tested: opencode serve --pure
```

Command used to start the server:

```bash
OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode serve --pure --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 19322 --print-logs --log-level WARN
```

Repro stress loop:

```bash
server_pid=$(pgrep -f 'opencode serve --pure --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 19322' | head -1)

for round in $(seq 1 45); do
  for i in $(seq 1 250); do
    timeout 0.1 curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:19322/event >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    timeout 0.1 curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:19322/global/event >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  done
  wait
  sleep 1
  rss=$(ps -o rss= -p "$server_pid" | tr -d ' ')
  fds=$(ls /proc/$server_pid/fd 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  states=$(ss -tanp 2>/dev/null | rg ':19322' | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | xargs)
  printf 'round=%02d rss_kb=%s rss_mb=%s fds=%s states=%s\n' "$round" "$rss" "$((rss/1024))" "$fds" "$states"
  if [ -n "$rss" ] && [ "$rss" -gt 2100000 ]; then break; fi
done
```

Observed RSS growth:

```text
round=01 rss_kb=393784  rss_mb=384  fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 480 TIME-WAIT
round=05 rss_kb=560208  rss_mb=547  fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 2399 TIME-WAIT
round=10 rss_kb=810592  rss_mb=791  fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 4442 TIME-WAIT
round=15 rss_kb=1052384 rss_mb=1027 fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 5937 TIME-WAIT
round=20 rss_kb=1283072 rss_mb=1253 fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 7318 TIME-WAIT
round=25 rss_kb=1585204 rss_mb=1548 fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 8247 TIME-WAIT
round=30 rss_kb=1847936 rss_mb=1804 fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 8605 TIME-WAIT
round=35 rss_kb=2120868 rss_mb=2071 fds=25 states=1 LISTEN 8951 TIME-WAIT
```

Notes:

- FD count stayed flat at 25.
- I did not see `CLOSE_WAIT`; the sockets were `TIME-WAIT` plus the listening socket.
- RSS did not require an active established connection count to keep growing.
- A simple `/health` short-request control from an earlier run also grew RSS, but much less: about +30 MB for roughly 1200 requests. The SSE endpoints grew far faster.

Great PR — this is exactly the fix I've been looking for.

I independently diagnosed the same root cause: when pasting a file path from the system clipboard into OpenCode's TUI, the `pasteInputText()` handler auto-detects it as a local file and converts it to an attachment reference instead of inserting the literal path text. The `text/plain` clipboard content is correct (verified via `xclip`), so the issue is entirely in how OpenCode processes the pasted content.

Adding `Ctrl+Alt+V` as a plain-text paste bypass is a clean solution — it preserves the existing image/attachment paste behavior on `Ctrl+V` while giving users an explicit escape hatch for when they need the path as text. 

Tested scenario this fixes: "copy a file path from VS Code Explorer → paste into OpenCode → path gets replaced with a file reference like `PDF 1` instead of the actual full path".

Looking forward to seeing this merged!
